summary.text: Martin Luther was a German priest, theologian and professor who became the central figure of the Protestant Reformation.
He rejected Catholic teachings on indulgences and papal authority, and in 1517 he wrote the Ninety-five Theses to start an international debate.
He taught that justification is a free gift of God's grace received through faith, and that the Bible is the only source of divinely revealed knowledge.

facts.label: German Bible
facts.value: His 1534 translation made scripture far more accessible to laypeople

facts.label: Excommunication
facts.value: Pope Leo X excommunicated him in January 1521

facts.label: Marriage
facts.value: His marriage to Katharina von Bora set a model for clerical marriage

items.prompt: In 1535 a German farmer wants to read scripture himself, in the language he speaks. Which of Luther's works helped most?

options.label: His hymns, used in Protestant church singing
The Ninety-five Theses, posted on a church door
His German translation of the Bible, finished in 1534
His writings against the pope's authority

items.explain: Luther's German translation made the Bible vastly more accessible to the laity and shaped German culture.

items.prompt: A neighbor insists that people win God's favor through their own deeds and merit. How would Luther answer?

options.label: God gives it freely as grace, received through faith
Good deeds are worthless and should be avoided
Merit counts if a priest approves each good deed
Faith matters little compared with steady charity

items.explain: Luther taught that justification is not earned by human acts or merit but received as the free gift of God's grace through faith, though he held good works to be a necessary fruit of living faith.

items.prompt: A bishop says only the Church hierarchy can define what Christians must believe. Which of Luther's teachings challenged that?

options.label: Tradition and councils carry equal weight with scripture
Only the pope may interpret the Gospel for believers
Human reason alone is enough to lead people to God
The Bible is the only source of divinely revealed knowledge

items.explain: Luther taught that the Bible is the only source of divinely revealed knowledge on the Gospel, which challenged the authority of the pope and bishops.

items.prompt: In 1520 Pope Leo X demanded that Luther renounce all his writings, and Luther refused. What did the pope do?

options.label: Sent him to live in a monastery for life
Excommunicated him from the Church
Had him tried and condemned as an outlaw
Made him a bishop to win him over

items.explain: Leo X excommunicated Luther in January 1521. It was the emperor, Charles V, who later condemned him as an outlaw at the Diet of Worms.

items.prompt: What did Luther's marriage to a former nun lead to?

options.label: It forced all Catholic clergy to marry
It sent nuns out of their convents
It set a model letting Protestant clergy marry
It ended the need for ordination

items.explain: His marriage to Katharina von Bora set a model for clerical marriage, allowing Protestant clergy to marry.

items.prompt: Luther's father was determined that his eldest son would become a lawyer. What did Luther do?

options.label: Finished his legal studies before turning to theology
Enrolled, then dropped out almost at once, doubting the work's certainty
Refused to attend university at all
Switched from legal studies to medicine

items.explain: Luther enrolled in law as his father wished but dropped out almost immediately, believing it an uncertain profession, and was drawn to theology and philosophy.
